# Secondary experiment on evidence sensitivity

The original FEVER development-set scores and the claim-only ceiling on the symmetric test set were known when designing this analysis. Model outputs for the following comparisons had not been examined. This is a secondary benchmark analysis.

Use all examples of the authors’ symmetric v0.2 development and test releases. Run the quantized Xenova ONNX conversions of BART-large-MNLI (revision 71a9d2a7c389b1a812afc3cc1668f8c877681b00) and RoBERTa-large-MNLI (f44e410851308d901c324c31af38793f50205e91) without training or parameter search. Input is the supplied evidence as premise and claim as hypothesis. Predict SUPPORTS for an entailment logit strictly greater than contradiction, REFUTES otherwise. The two-label challenge contains no neutral examples. Report the effect of allowing neutral as a third, always incorrect, prediction.

With identical logits, compare ordinary independent classification, a decoder imposing an equal label count within each exact claim string, and a joint decoder imposing equal counts for both claim and evidence strings. This last decoder maximizes summed entailment-minus-contradiction scores by a binary linear program. Balance is an assumption about this benchmark's construction. Inspect whether gold satisfies it only after decoding. An odd-sized group or infeasible system must be reported for that split. Never use gold counts to set quotas. A comparison with ordinary classification changes the inference information available (items are observed as a batch). Report raw correct counts, all-correct claim groups, rescues, regressions and model input hashes. Retain all comparisons in both splits. Shared strings connect rows so casewise significance tests are inappropriate. This does not propose the balanced decoder for live fact checking.

Run instructions and attribution accompany the manuscript. The decision metric is published-label binary accuracy on the complete release. Using exact evidence strings for grouping is part of the experimental treatment. No evidence retrieval or new human judgments take place.

## Transfer to VitaminC

After inspecting dataset schema and aggregate label patterns, use real-revision examples in the official test release. Retain all rows for the first 128 page titles sorted by SHA-256 of UTF-8 title (1,622 examples). Before inspecting model scores, fix the primary comparator to the authors’ ALBERT-base-VitaminC-FEVER checkpoint with their evidence–claim order, 256-token limit and full three-label space. Independently classify each example. Within each (case ID, exact claim) group of size two, also evaluate a paired decision that requires exactly one SUPPORTS prediction; choose the assignment of maximum summed logits, allowing either REFUTES or NOT ENOUGH INFO for the other example. Use ordinary decisions for all remaining groups. This compares two information regimes at scoring time. Report both regressions and rescues, coverage, per-page bootstrap difference (row-weighted), and the number of gold groups violating the constraint. Do not tune thresholds or remove violations. Coverage applies to observed paired revisions only. The structural composition of this dataset was already known, so this is a transfer test of the decision rule and not blinded discovery.
